lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 138: Enter in the search box now jumps to the results.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one thirty-eight: Enter in the search box now jumps to the results.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Enter in the search box now moves the focus to the results. The change is a new branch, a small getter and a crash guard.
You press Ctrl+F and type a word, and the results update as you type.
lines.say: You press Control F and type a word, and the results update as you type.

lines.caption: When you press Enter, the box checks whether its text is a search. If it is, it takes a new branch.
That holds whether you used Ctrl+F or typed the search into the location bar yourself, a case CI's second review found.
lines.say: That holds whether you used Control F or typed the search into the location bar yourself, a case C I's second review found.

lines.caption: Only in search mode does the branch first disarm a handler, so the location bar stays a search when the focus leaves it.
Then it moves the keyboard focus to the file list.
Down now selects the first match, using the list's own keys, and the search stays on screen.
Enter on a folder or file path still works exactly as before.
Before, Enter did nothing in the search box, and you needed Tab twice to reach the results.
Search runs on every keystroke, so Enter's only new job is moving the keyboard to the results.
Without the disarm step, the path-buttons bar would swap back to buttons in the middle of a search.
The focus call is the same one the location bar already makes after selecting a file, from issue 93.
lines.say: The focus call is the same one the location bar already makes after selecting a file, from issue ninety-three.

lines.caption: The whole change is this new branch in the Enter handler, plus a getter that says whether the window is searching.
A one-line guard in the path entry now cancels a search only when the box is inside a Thunar window.
Without it, after Enter on a hand-typed search, the old box left the window, and the next folder change crashed Thunar.
One thing differs from the issue: Ctrl+F during a search turns it off. You decided to keep it that way.
lines.say: One thing differs from the issue: Control F during a search turns it off. You decided to keep it that way.

lines.caption: The PR changes four source files and adds a verify script and this page.
To undo it, revert the PR. Nothing else depends on it.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was tested locally and in CI, reviewed locally and twice by CI, and audited. The script's newest step found a crash, now fixed.
lines.say: It was tested locally and in C I, reviewed locally and twice by C I, and audited. The script's newest step found a crash, now fixed.

lines.caption: It reuses an existing focus call, and the issue had already shown the list's Down key works in search results.
Locally, the debs were built and installed, and all 29 verify tests passed, twice, before CI's two fixes.
lines.say: Locally, the debs were built and installed, and all twenty-nine verify tests passed, twice, before C I's two fixes.

lines.caption: The new script checked that Enter, then Down, selects exactly apple1.txt.
lines.say: The new script checked that Enter, then Down, selects exactly apple one dot t x t.

lines.caption: It checked that the search stays after Enter, with both bar styles; for the buttons bar, a screenshot shows the text box stays.
And with no matches, Enter and Down leave Thunar running.
Ctrl+F after Enter was read in the code, not tested: it turns the search off.
lines.say: Control F after Enter was read in the code, not tested: it turns the search off.

lines.caption: CI built the debs before its second fix, and all 29 verify tests passed, with new shots of Enter and the buttons bar.
lines.say: C I built the debs before its second fix, and all twenty-nine verify tests passed, with new shots of Enter and the buttons bar.

lines.caption: An independent auditor looked at all 172 screenshots from that run and passed every one.
lines.say: An independent auditor looked at all one hundred seventy-two screenshots from that run and passed every one.

lines.caption: Before that fix, a local run of the full suite passed 28 of 29: the new hand-typed step crashed Thunar.
lines.say: Before that fix, a local run of the full suite passed twenty-eight of twenty-nine: the new hand-typed step crashed Thunar.

lines.caption: A debugger trace put the crash in the path entry's changed handler.
A new last step types a search by hand, then Enter and Down. With the fix it passed locally; the debs without it crashed.
The full suite with the fix runs in CI on the next push. It has not run yet.
CI rendered an earlier version of this page and found the narration current. The narrated video has not run.
lines.say: C I rendered an earlier version of this page and found the narration current. The narrated video has not run.

lines.caption: A local review before the first push found three things.
One was a real bug with the path-buttons bar. It was fixed, and the script tests that layout.
A missing check was skipped as a nit, and the missing explainer is this page.
CI's own review then found three more.
The medium one, a search text getting stuck, was fixed by CI's own commit.
You accepted the two low ones: a check shown by a screenshot, not asserted, and a handler with no visible effect.
CI's second review found four more.
lines.say: C I's second review found four more.

lines.caption: The medium one: Enter on a hand-typed search no longer moved the focus. CI's own commit fixed it.
lines.say: The medium one: Enter on a hand-typed search no longer moved the focus. C I's own commit fixed it.

lines.caption: You accepted an old upstream quirk: a hand-typed search can't be cancelled with Escape.
A missing test of a hand-typed search was added to the script, and that step found the crash.
And a misplaced accept line, with no effect on the code, was accepted under the repo's rule for low findings.
So four findings were accepted, not fixed, and the three that mattered for the code are fixed.
Your installed Thunar gets the change with the next package built from main.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one, and the Ctrl+F question is settled.
lines.say: No open issue depends on this one, and the Control F question is settled.

lines.caption: You decided to keep Ctrl+F as it is: it turns a search off, and a click returns to the search box.
lines.say: You decided to keep Control F as it is: it turns a search off, and a click returns to the search box.

lines.caption: So no follow-up issue is filed.
In short: type a search, press Enter, then Down, and you're on the first match.
